headline: What changed at the IRS this week, and what it means for you
intro: The short version for anyone holding an IRS letter or sitting on unfiled returns. Every item links to the IRS or a named source.
take: Most weeks the IRS changes very little that touches an ordinary taxpayer with a notice. This is one of those weeks, and I would rather tell you that than invent urgency.

What does not change: the deadlines printed on your letter. Open it, write down the date, and answer before it. Everything else can be fixed with a former examiner on your side, but a missed deadline cannot.

items.html: 7% through Dec. 31, unchanged from last quarter (IRS, Aug. 21). No 2027 first-quarter rate was on the IRS news list as of Nov. 10.
The permanent charitable deduction for people who do not itemize begins with 2026 gifts: up to $1,000 single / $2,000 joint, cash only (IR-2026-135).
Tax pros can now make certain payments for business clients through Tax Pro Account. Individual rules are unchanged (IR-2026-134).
The official 2027 tax brackets were released (IR-2026-133). See our 2027 brackets page.

fine: Not tax advice. Each topic page has its own raw example and what is new for that topic.
faq_answer: As of Nov. 12, 2026: interest on unpaid tax stays at 7% through Dec. 31; the IRS released 2027 tax brackets on Nov. 5; a permanent charitable deduction for non-itemizers ($1,000 single, $2,000 joint, cash only) starts with 2026 gifts; and tax pros can now make certain payments for business clients through Tax Pro Account. Romeo Razi, CPA, a former IRS Tax Examiner, says none of this changes what to do if you have a notice: open it, note the date, and respond before the deadline.
